claim: The Notch-Delta pathway is required to distinguish target from non-target muscles in C. elegans egg-laying circuit.
source_text: We found that the Notch-Delta pathway was required to distinguish target from non-target muscles.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental results showing mutations in Notch-Delta pathway components affect muscle target selection.

claim: APX-1/Delta acts in surrounding cells including the non-target vm1 to activate LIN-12/Notch in the target vm2.
source_text: APX-1/Delta acts in surrounding cells including the non-target vm1 to activate LIN-12/Notch in the target vm2.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific expression and rescue experiments showing APX-1 expression pattern and LIN-12 activation.

claim: LIN-12 functions cell-autonomously to up-regulate the expression of UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 in vm2.
source_text: LIN-12 functions cell-autonomously to up-regulate the expression of UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 in vm2, which in turn function together to promote muscle arm formation and guidance.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by mosaic analysis, cell-specific rescue experiments, and expression pattern analysis showing LIN-12-dependent regulation.

claim: Ectopic expression of UNC-40/DCC in non-target vm1 muscle is sufficient to induce muscle arm extension from these cells.
source_text: Ectopic expression of UNC-40/DCC in non-target vm1 muscle is sufficient to induce muscle arm extension from these cells.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic experiments showing ectopic UNC-40 expression induces muscle arm-like structures in vm1.

claim: The C. elegans egg-laying circuit consists of four type 1 vulval muscle cells (vm1) and four type 2 vulval muscle cells (vm2).
source_text: The C. elegans egg-laying circuit consists four type 1 vulval muscle cells (vm1) and four type 2 vulval muscle cells (vm2), which form two X-shaped structures near the vulval opening
evidence_reasoning: Based on established anatomical knowledge of C. elegans and cited EM reconstruction work.

claim: HSN and VC4/5 motoneurons form synapses exclusively on vm2 but not vm1.
source_text: the egg-laying motoneurons HSN and VC4/5 form serotoninergic and cholinergic chemical synapses exclusively on vm2
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited EM reconstruction and confirmed by fluorescent imaging in this study.

claim: vm2 cells extend dendritic spine-like muscle arms laterally on which they receive synapses with HSN and VC neurons.
source_text: Each of the four vm2 cells extends a dendritic spine-like muscle arm laterally, on which it receives synapses with HSN and VC neurons
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescent imaging and consistent with EM reconstruction data.

claim: UNC-103E potassium channel is enriched on vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: low level of transgenic expression of UNC-103E::GFP with an integrated single-copy transgene showed that UNC-103E was dramatically enriched on vm2 muscle arms
evidence_reasoning: Shown through single-copy transgene expression and fluorescence imaging.

claim: HSN neurons are not required for vm2 specification and muscle arm development.
source_text: in all of the examined animals, the morphology and position of vm2 muscle arms were indistinguishable from the wild type counterparts
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated in egl-1(n986) mutants where HSN neurons undergo programmed cell death but vm2 muscle arms develop normally.

claim: VC neurons are not required for vm2 muscle arm development.
source_text: in a portion of the egl-1(n986);lin-39(n709) double mutant animals which lacked both HSN and VC neurons, the vm2 muscle arms still existed
evidence_reasoning: Shown through genetic ablation experiments in double mutants.

claim: Synaptic vesicles are not required for vm2 muscle arm development.
source_text: in unc-104(e1265) mutant animals, in which the synaptic vesicles were absent from the presynaptic regions in both HSN and VC neurons, vm2 muscle arm development was not affected
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through analysis of unc-104 mutants lacking synaptic vesicle transport.

claim: Vulval epithelial cells are required for normal vulval muscle differentiation and morphogenesis.
source_text: we examined the vm2 muscle arm morphology in lin-3(e1417) mutant animals, in which vulval epithelial cell fate is abnormal, and observed severe defects on both vulval muscle morphology and muscle arm development
evidence_reasoning: Shown through analysis of lin-3 mutants with abnormal vulval epithelial cell fate.

claim: lin-12(wy750) is a missense mutation (G473R) in one of the conserved extracellular EGF domains of the LIN-12 protein.
source_text: Sequence analyses revealed that lin-12(wy750) contained a single missense mutation (G473R) in one of the conserved extracellular EGF domains of the LIN-12 protein
evidence_reasoning: Determined through DNA sequencing of the mutant allele.

claim: lin-12(wy750) is a loss-of-function allele.
source_text: Two additional results indicated that lin-12(wy750) was a loss-of-function allele.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by complementation tests and genomic rescue experiments.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants show complete absence of vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: the SER-1B::GFP labeled vm2 muscle arm structures were completely absent
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescence imaging of multiple markers in mutant animals.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants have normal vulval morphogenesis.
source_text: we found no vulval morphogenesis defect in lin-12(wy750) mutants either by differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy or the localization pattern of the ajm-1::gfp apical junction marker
evidence_reasoning: Shown through DIC microscopy and apical junction marker analysis at multiple developmental stages.

claim: apx-1(wy755) and sel-12(wy760) mutants show similar vm2 muscle arm defects to lin-12(wy750).
source_text: Two other mutants isolated from the same screen, apx-1(wy750) and sel-12(wy760), were very similar to the lin-12(wy750) mutant in their specific defective vm2 muscle arm development and normal vulval muscle development
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis of independently isolated mutant alleles.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants lay fewer eggs compared to wild-type animals.
source_text: the muscle arm defective mutants laid notably fewer eggs compared to the wild-type animals
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through egg-laying assays comparing mutant and wild-type animals.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants retain more late-stage embryos compared to wild-type animals.
source_text: the muscle arm defective mutants retained more late-stage embryos compared to the wild-type animals
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through analysis of embryo stages in freshly-laid eggs.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants have asynchronous vulval muscle Ca2+ transients.
source_text: double Ca2+ transients were often asynchronous, with significant delays between anterior and posterior vulval muscle transients that resulted in uncoordinated vulval muscle contractions that were not able to release eggs
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ratiometric Ca2+ imaging in behaving animals.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants have a twofold increase in the frequency of Ca2+ transient peaks compared to wild type.
source_text: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants had a twofold increase in the frequency of Ca2+ transient peaks
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through analysis of Ca2+ imaging recordings.

claim: The average anterior/posterior delay in double Ca2+ transients increased from ~100 ms in wild type to ~800 ms in lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants.
source_text: In wild-type animals, the average anterior/posterior delay was only ∼100 ms...In both lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants, the average anterior/posterior delay in double Ca2+ transients increased to ∼800 ms
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through temporal analysis of Ca2+ transient peaks.

claim: vm2 muscle arms are required for synchronous excitation of anterior and posterior vulval muscles needed for successful egg-laying behavior.
source_text: these results show that the vm2 muscle arms lacking in lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants are not necessary for excitation of the vulval muscles, but suggest they are required for the synchronous excitation of anterior and posterior vulval muscles needed to successfully execute egg-laying behavior
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from Ca2+ imaging data showing asynchronous activation in mutants lacking muscle arms.

claim: lin-12(wy750) represents a partial loss-of-function allele.
source_text: it is likely that the missense mutation we isolated represents a partial loss-of-function allele
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the specific phenotype compared to null alleles that cause lethality and severe vulval defects.

claim: Muscle arm development requires a higher level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity compared with earlier developmental events.
source_text: muscle arm development might require a higher level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity compared with earlier developmental events
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the observation that partial loss-of-function alleles specifically affect muscle arm development but not earlier events.

claim: LIN-12/Notch signaling is required at the L4 stage for vm2 muscle arm development.
source_text: More than 80% of the animals still showed defective muscle arms when shifted from 25°C to 15°C at mid-L4
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through temperature shift experiments using temperature-sensitive alleles.

claim: LIN-12/Notch function in vm2 muscle arm development is independent of its earlier roles in AC/VU decision and VPC specification.
source_text: This lin-12 function is independent of other known roles of lin-12, all of which occur prior to early-L4 stage.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from temperature shift experiments showing late requirement and normal early developmental events in weak alleles.

claim: LIN-12 functions cell-autonomously in vm2 to regulate muscle arm development.
source_text: These results indicate that lin-12 functions cell-autonomously in vm2 to regulate the muscle arm development.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through mosaic analysis showing rescue only when LIN-12 is expressed in vm2.

claim: APX-1 is expressed in secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells.
source_text: we found that apx-1 was expressed in the secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells
evidence_reasoning: Shown through expression pattern analysis using APX-1 reporter constructs.

claim: APX-1 functions non-cell-autonomously to regulate vm2 muscle arm development.
source_text: apx-1 functions non-cell-autonomously to regulate the vm2 muscle arm development
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific rescue experiments showing rescue when APX-1 is expressed in surrounding cells but not vm2.

claim: vm2 muscle arms directly contact primary and secondary vulval epithelial cells.
source_text: the muscle arms are located between the 1o and the 2o vulval epithelial cells and directly contact these cells
evidence_reasoning: Shown through confocal imaging of muscle arms and epithelial cell markers.

claim: SEL-12 functions cell-autonomously in vm2 to regulate muscle arm development.
source_text: expression of sel-12 in vulval muscle cells completely rescued the vm2 muscle arm phenotype of sel-12(wy760)
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: Expression of dominant-negative LAG-1 in vulval muscles phenocopies muscle arm defects observed in lin-12, apx-1, and sel-12 mutants.
source_text: specific expression of a dominant-negative lag-1 construct in the vulval muscles phenocopied the muscle arm defects observed in lin-12(wy750), apx-1(wy750) and sel-12(wy760) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic expression of dominant-negative construct.

claim: The canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway controls transcription of downstream genes to regulate muscle arm development.
source_text: suggesting that the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway is likely involved by controlling the transcription of downstream genes
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from dominant-negative LAG-1 experiments and transcriptional reporter analyses.

claim: hlh-29 is a target gene of the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
source_text: the expression of a hlh-29 transcription reporter (hlh-29::gfp), a known target gene of the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2, was also dramatically down-regulated in lin-12(wy750), apx-1(wy755) and sel-12(wy760) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transcriptional reporter analysis and consistent with known Notch target genes.

claim: APX-1 promotes lin-12 expression in vm2 cells.
source_text: apx-1(wy755) mutant animals showed significantly reduced expression of lin-12 in vm2 cells
evidence_reasoning: Shown through LIN-12 reporter expression analysis in apx-1 mutants.

claim: apx-1 expression does not change in lin-12(wy750) mutants.
source_text: we did not observe any change of apx-1 expression in the lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through APX-1 reporter expression analysis in lin-12 mutants.

claim: APX-1 unilaterally promotes lin-12 expression and activates the LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
source_text: These results argue that apx-1 unilaterally promotes lin-12 expression and activates the LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from asymmetric regulation pattern where APX-1 affects LIN-12 but not vice versa.

claim: The lin-12 promoter contains three LAG-1 consensus binding sites.
source_text: we found three LAG-1 consensus binding sites in the promoter region of lin-12
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis of the lin-12 promoter region.

claim: lin-12(e2621) contains a 541-bp deletion in the promoter region that removes two LAG-1 binding sites.
source_text: We sequenced the lin-12 promoter in this allele and found a 541-bp deletion in the promoter region leading to the deletion of two of the three LAG-1 binding sites
evidence_reasoning: Determined through DNA sequencing of the mutant allele.

claim: lin-12(e2621) shows muscle arm defects without vulval morphogenesis phenotype.
source_text: One lin-12 loss-of-function allele, e2621, was previously known to have egg-laying defects without vulval morphogenesis phenotype...the muscle arm development was similarly affected in lin-12(e2621)
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis and consistent with previous reports.

claim: Muscle arm development requires positive transcriptional feedback of the LIN-12/Notch pathway.
source_text: suggesting that the muscle arm development might require the positive transcriptional feedback of the LIN-12/Notch pathway
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the muscle arm defects in lin-12(e2621) which lacks LAG-1 binding sites in the promoter.

claim: UNC-40 is a homolog of Deleted in Colorectal Carcinoma (DCC) and neogenin in vertebrates.
source_text: UNC-40, which is a homolog of Deleted in Colorectal Carcinoma (DCC) and neogenin in vertebrates serving as a receptor for the UNC-6/Netrin ligand
evidence_reasoning: Based on established molecular homology and cited literature.

claim: UNC-40 has been shown to regulate axon guidance and promote presynaptic assembly in C. elegans.
source_text: UNC-40/DCC, the receptor of UNC-6/Netrin, has been shown to regulate axon guidance toward ventral UNC-6 as well as locally promote presynaptic assembly in the C. elegans interneuron AIY
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited previous studies.

claim: UNC-40 plays critical roles in the formation of dendritic spine-like postsynaptic muscle arms of body wall muscles in worms.
source_text: UNC-40 plays critical roles in the formation of dendritic spine-like postsynaptic muscle arms of the body wall muscles in worms
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited previous studies.

claim: UNC-40's function in body wall muscle arm formation appears to be independent of UNC-6.
source_text: this function appears to be independent of UNC-6
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited previous studies.

claim: unc-40(e271) and madd-2(ok2226) mutants show vm2 muscle arm defects.
source_text: unc-40(e271) and madd-2(ok2226) show missing (middle) or abnormal (right) muscle arm phenotypes
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis of mutant animals.

claim: UNC-40 is preferentially expressed in vm2 cells and enriched on muscle arms in wild type.
source_text: UNC-40::GFP is preferentially expressed in vm2 and enriched on the muscle arms in the wild type
evidence_reasoning: Shown through translational reporter expression analysis.

claim: UNC-40 expression is down-regulated in lin-12(wy750) mutants.
source_text: UNC-40::GFP is preferentially expressed in vm2 and enriched on the muscle arms in the wild type, and is down-regulated in the lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through translational reporter expression analysis in mutants.

claim: MADD-2 is preferentially expressed in vm2 cells in wild type.
source_text: MADD-2::GFP is preferentially expressed in vm2 in the wild type
evidence_reasoning: Shown through translational reporter expression analysis.

claim: MADD-2 expression is down-regulated in apx-1(wy755) mutants.
source_text: MADD-2::GFP is preferentially expressed in vm2 in the wild type, and is down-regulated in the apx-1 (wy755) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through translational reporter expression analysis in mutants.

claim: unc-40 is preferentially transcribed in vm2 in wild type and down-regulated in lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: unc-40 is preferentially transcribed in vm2 in wild type, and down-regulated in lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through transcriptional reporter analysis.

claim: madd-2 is preferentially transcribed in vm2 in wild type and down-regulated in lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: madd-2 is preferentially transcribed in vm2 in wild type, and down-regulated in lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through transcriptional reporter analysis.

claim: The canonical LIN-12/Notch signaling pathway acts to promote the transcriptions of both unc-40 and madd-2.
source_text: These data indicate that the canonical LIN-12/Notch signaling pathway acts to promote the transcriptions of both unc-40 and madd-2 directly.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from transcriptional reporter analyses showing LIN-12-dependent transcription.

claim: Two LAG-1 consensus binding sites are found on the proximal promoter region of the madd-2 gene.
source_text: two LAG-1 consensus binding sites were found on the proximal promoter region of the madd-2 gene
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis of the madd-2 promoter.

claim: Two LAG-1 binding sites are found in the third intron of unc-40 that is essential for its expression.
source_text: two were found in the third intron of unc-40 that is essential for its expression
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis and confirmed through personal communication.

claim: Forced expression of UNC-40 in vm2 from the unc-103e promoter induces the formation of muscle arms in the lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: the forced expression of UNC-40 in vm2 from the unc-103e promoter induces the formation of muscle arms in the lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: Ectopic expression of UNC-40 in vm1 induces muscle arm-like membrane extensions.
source_text: the ectopic expression of UNC-40 in vm1 induces the muscle arm-like membrane extensions
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ectopic expression experiments using vm1-specific promoter.

claim: Misexpression of UNC-40 is sufficient to induce dendritic spine-like membrane extensions from vm1 cells.
source_text: we found that misexpression of UNC-40 was sufficient to induce the dendritic spine-like membrane extensions from vm1 cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ectopic expression experiments.

claim: Ectopic muscle arms from vm1 always form from the medial surface of vm1, the identical location as for normal vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: the vm1 muscle arms always formed from the medial surface of vm1, the identical location as for the normal vm2 muscle arms
evidence_reasoning: Observed through imaging of ectopic expression experiments.

claim: UNC-40 responds to specific environmental cues to guide the formation of muscle arms.
source_text: suggesting that UNC-40 responds to specific environmental cues to guide the formation of muscle arms
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the stereotyped location of ectopic muscle arms despite ectopic UNC-40 expression.

claim: Ectopic expression of madd-2 in vm1 is not able to induce muscle arm formation.
source_text: Similar ectopic expression of madd-2 in vm1 was not able to induce muscle arm formation
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ectopic expression experiments showing no phenotype.

claim: unc-40(n324); madd-2(ok2226) double mutants show slightly enhanced muscle arm defects compared to single mutants.
source_text: We generated an unc-40(n324); madd-2(ok2226) double mutant and found slightly enhanced muscle arm defects in the double mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis of double mutants.

claim: Overexpression of madd-2 partially rescues the muscle arm defects of unc-40(n324) null mutant.
source_text: the overexpression of madd-2 partially rescued the muscle arm defects of unc-40(n324) null mutant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic overexpression experiments.

claim: Overexpression of unc-40 largely rescues the muscle arm defects of madd-2(ok2226) mutant.
source_text: overexpression of unc-40 largely rescued the muscle arm defects of madd-2(ok2226) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic overexpression experiments.

claim: madd-2 functions synergistically with unc-40 to promote muscle arm formation.
source_text: suggesting that madd-2 likely functioned synergistically with unc-40 to promote muscle arm formation
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from genetic interaction and rescue experiments.

claim: Expression of madd-2 and unc-40 is not mutually regulated.
source_text: Expression of madd-2 and unc-40 is not mutually regulated
evidence_reasoning: Shown through expression analysis in respective mutants.

claim: unc-40 and madd-2 at least partly function in parallel.
source_text: consistent to the hypothesis that unc-40 and madd-2 at least partly function in parallel
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from lack of mutual regulation and genetic interaction data.

claim: unc-40, potentiated by madd-2, plays a deterministic role in guiding muscle arm extension and postsynaptic target selection.
source_text: these results demonstrate that unc-40, potentiated by madd-2, plays a deterministic role in guiding the muscle arm extension and the postsynaptic target selection
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from combined genetic, expression, and ectopic expression experiments.

claim: The formation of pre- and postsynaptic specializations in the egg-laying circuit can occur at different times.
source_text: First, the formation of pre- and postsynaptic specializations can occur at different times. The HSN presynaptic specializations form at the early L4 stage, significantly before the maturation of the postsynaptic targets.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through developmental time course observations.

claim: The development of pre- and postsynaptic specializations appears to be independent of each other.
source_text: Second, the development of the pre- and postsynaptic specializations appears to be independent of each other.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ablation experiments showing normal development in absence of partner cells.

claim: Eliminating postsynaptic cells does not affect the timing and location of synaptic vesicle accumulation in HSN neurons.
source_text: Eliminating the postsynaptic cells does not affect the timing and location of synaptic vesicle accumulation in HSN neurons
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited previous work.

claim: Ablation of presynaptic neurons has no obvious effect on the timing and direction of muscle arm growth.
source_text: ablation of the presynaptic neurons has no obvious effect on the timing and direction of the muscle arm growth
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic ablation experiments in this study.

claim: Primary vulval epithelial cells serve as guidepost cells for HSN presynaptic development.
source_text: we previously found that the primary vulval epithelial cells serve as guidepost cells for the HSN presynaptic development
evidence_reasoning: Based on authors' previous published work.

claim: Primary vulval epithelial cells express SYG-2, which clusters and activates SYG-1 on the HSN axon.
source_text: These primary cells express a transmembrane IgSF protein SYG-2, which clusters and activates a related molecule, SYG-1 on the HSN axon.
evidence_reasoning: Based on authors' previous published work.

claim: The intercellular interaction between SYG-1 and SYG-2 defines the location of HSN synapses and initiates presynaptic formation.
source_text: The intercellular interaction between SYG-1 and SYG-2 defines the location of HSN synapses and initiates the presynaptic formation
evidence_reasoning: Based on authors' previous published work.

claim: Postsynaptic differentiation is likely guided by the secondary vulval epithelial cells.
source_text: postsynaptic differentiation is likely guided by the secondary vulval epithelial cells
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from APX-1 expression pattern and cell contact observations.

claim: The muscle arms appear to grow along the interface between the primary and the secondary vulval epithelial cells through an UNC-40-dependent mechanism.
source_text: The muscle arms appear to grow along the interface between the primary and the secondary vulval epithelial cells through possibly an UNC-40-dependent mechanism
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from imaging data showing muscle arm position and UNC-40 function.

claim: Epithelial cells play organizational roles for the development of the entire vulval organ, coordinating multiple events.
source_text: The epithelial cells not only function as the channel for egg-laying but also play organizational roles for the development of the entire vulval organ, coordinating multiple events including vulval muscle migration, axon guidance of HSN, VC axon branching and synapse formation.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the multiple roles of epithelial cells demonstrated in this and previous studies.

claim: Vulval morphogenesis requires a low level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activation, while vm2 postsynaptic specification requires a relatively high level.
source_text: these data strongly argue that vulval morphogenesis requires a low level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activation, while vm2 postsynaptic specification requires a relatively high level of LIN-12/Notch activity
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the differential effects of partial loss-of-function alleles on different developmental processes.

claim: vm1 and vm2 are from a common lineage and are physically adjacent.
source_text: While vm1 and vm2 are from a common lineage, are physically adjacent and share many molecular components
evidence_reasoning: Based on established developmental biology knowledge of C. elegans.

claim: vm1 is mainly controlled by vm2 via gap junctions.
source_text: vm1 is mainly controlled by vm2 via gap junctions
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited EM reconstruction work.

claim: vm2 receives some additional synapses with the ventral nerve cord besides HSN and VC4/5.
source_text: Besides forming major synaptic connection on HSN and VC4/5, vm2 also receive some additional synapses with the ventral nerve cord
evidence_reasoning: Based on personal communication cited in the manuscript.

claim: HSN axon guidance and presynaptic formation precede both axon growth of VC neurons and vulval muscle differentiation.
source_text: Developmental studies showed that HSN axon guidance and presynaptic formation preceded both axon growth of VC neurons and vulval muscle differentiation
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through developmental time course observations.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants have normal VC4 and VC5 axon morphology.
source_text: Both HSN and VC presynaptic markers appeared normal in the lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Shown through imaging of presynaptic markers in mutants.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants have normal HSN presynaptic specializations.
source_text: Both HSN and VC presynaptic markers appeared normal in the lin-12(wy750) mutant, indicating that the mutation specifically affected postsynaptic differentiation and development
evidence_reasoning: Shown through imaging of presynaptic markers in mutants.

claim: Vulval muscles are produced through three rounds of cell divisions from a single sex myoblast cell derived from the postembryonic mesodermal lineage (M lineage).
source_text: Vulval muscles, together with the uterine muscles, are produced through three rounds of cell divisions from a single sex myoblast cell, which is derived from the postembryonic mesodermal lineage (M lineage).
evidence_reasoning: Based on established developmental biology knowledge of C. elegans.

claim: hlh-8::gfp is specifically expressed in undifferentiated cells of M lineage.
source_text: the hlh-8::gfp that is specifically expressed in undifferentiated cells of M lineage
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited characterization of the marker.

claim: egl-15::gfp is exclusively expressed in vm1 cells in the egg-laying system.
source_text: an egl-15::gfp reporter which is exclusively expressed in vm1 cells in egg-laying system
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited characterization of the marker.

claim: rgs-2::gfp labels uterine muscles.
source_text: We also examined rgs-2::gfp that labeled uterine muscles
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited characterization of the marker.

claim: In lin-12(wy750) mutants, hlh-8::gfp, egl-15::gfp, and rgs-2::gfp exhibit wild type patterns.
source_text: In lin-12(wy750) mutants, all three markers exhibits wild type pattern
evidence_reasoning: Shown through marker expression analysis in mutants.

claim: Many molecular signatures of the M lineage are intact in lin-12(wy750) mutants.
source_text: suggesting that many molecular signatures of the M lineage are intact in the lin-12(wy750) mutants, while the development of the postsynaptic specializations completely fails
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from normal expression of multiple lineage markers despite muscle arm defects.

claim: The position where vm1 is linked to the body wall is always on the dorsal side of the connection between vm2 and body wall in both wild type and lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: In both wild type and lin-12(wy750) mutant, the position where vm1 is linked to the body wall is always on the dorsal side of the connection between vm2 and body wall.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through quantitative morphological analysis.

claim: No significant difference was found in the intersection angle between vulval muscle and vulval slit between wild type and lin-12(wy750).
source_text: No significant difference was found on the intersection angle between the vulval muscle and the vulval slit
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through quantitative morphological measurements.

claim: No significant difference was found in the relative size of vm2 to vm1 (Svm2/Svm1) between wild type and lin-12(wy750).
source_text: No significant difference was found on...the relative size of vm2 to vm1 (Svm2/Svm1)
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through quantitative morphological measurements.

claim: The muscle defects in lin-12 mutants appear to be restricted to postsynaptic development in vm2 cells.
source_text: all these observations supports the notion that the muscle defects in lin-12 mutants appear to be restricted to the postsynaptic development in the vm2 cells
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from comprehensive analysis of multiple markers and morphological measurements.

claim: lin-12 and apx-1 weak loss-of-function alleles cause egg-laying defects due to the absence of vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: we definitively showed that the egg-laying defects in lin-12, apx-1, sel-12 weak loss-of-function alleles were due to the absence of vm2 muscle arm
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from combined phenotypic and functional analyses.

claim: LIN-12/Notch signaling instructs vulval organogenesis and synaptic development by regulating at least three sequential but independent developmental processes.
source_text: LIN-12/Notch signal instructs both vulval organogenesis and synaptic development of the egg-laying circuit by regulating at least three sequential but independent developmental processes: the AC/VU decision, in which LIN-12/Notch signaling promotes the differentiation of AC and VU cells; VPC specification, in which it determines the vulval precursor cell fates; and vm2 postsynaptic specification, in which it specifies the postsynaptic target cell and further regulates the muscle arm development.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from temporal analysis and comparison with known earlier functions of LIN-12/Notch.

claim: A novel ligand of UNC-40 functions in guiding muscle arm extension, distinct from UNC-6.
